body:
SOURCE-CHECKED DEMOLITION PASS 1 — strong spine; six corrections before this can become a plan.

I checked current main adf58cad3dc419d6a383355cf0479e846b5175dd against graph.scala, unit.scala, core span.scala, population.scala, codec/recall.scala, acquire/resolve.scala, segmenter.scala, interview/segment.scala, matrix.scala, signature.scala, and hsmm.scala.

WHAT I ACCEPT

- A1 structural well-formedness, A2 analysis admissibility, and A3 construction authority are genuinely separate.
- S1 is a real existing cartesian-product defect and a good independent correctness bead. SubjectAlignment can presently bind recall A to result B; PopulationAggregate catches it later. The positive factory and all four refusal doors can be populated now.
- S5 is the right joined-claim court.
- Bare RecallGraph JSON must remain structural only; a full construction artifact may regain authority only by recomputing every binding from bytes.
- The EventRecall reproduction, immediate safety label, and no-lattice-before-evidence rule stand.

BLOCK 1 — S2 mixes a cut with claims

OverlappingClaims is not a CutPolicy. It is a different ontology. A segmentation cut is an ordered set of contiguous transcript cells over an explicitly eligible region. Claims, repair scopes, discourse acts, and evidence supports may overlap or be discontinuous. Putting OverlappingClaims beside Partition and CoveringWithGaps creates one enum over two meanings.

Current source makes this concrete: RecallUnit.span is a SpanSet, and SpanSet is explicitly discontinuous evidence support. RecallGraph validates unit text against its hull. It cannot serve as the segmentation-cell representation.

Required separation:
- boundary plan: ordered contiguous cells plus explicit excluded/gap intervals;
- eligible-region mask: what part of this transcript the plan is obliged to cover;
- claim/support hypergraph: overlapping or discontinuous spans;
- interpretation evidence: SpanSet remains evidence.

The interview path proves why eligibility is first-class: InterviewSegmenter intentionally removes interviewer turns and crossing units. Partition of the full canonical transcript would reject that lawful task; partition of the declared participant-eligible regions can be judged.

Q1 answer: geometry is derived from the cells. Admission policy is named in configuration and receipt, and the factory proves the plan satisfies it. Same policy is necessary but not sufficient for comparability: alternatives must also share transcript checksum, eligible-region map, task/grain, and gap semantics.

BLOCK 2 — S3's Licence enum launders orthogonal coordinates

Heuristic, ProviderResolved, Calibrated, and Adjudicated are not four values of one dimension.

- heuristic/provider/adjudication describe construction route or evidence authority;
- Accepted/Alternatives/Unresolved/Rejected describe resolver outcome;
- calibrated describes whether a named calibration licenses probabilities;
- scientific admission is use-specific and derived from the preceding coordinates.

A provider-resolved artifact may be calibrated or uncalibrated. An adjudicated artifact can carry agreement and calibration evidence. One Licence phantom makes lawful combinations unrepresentable and false equivalences look settled.

Keep separate coordinates in one unforgeable artifact; derive a named admission witness for a declared scientific use. A phantom can enforce compile-time routing, but runtime receipts and a private validating decoder must carry and rederive the facts. The bare graph decoder at codec/recall.scala:260-276 should never mint any construction witness.

BLOCK 3 — S4 cannot reuse ClaimResolver wholesale

Q5 is fatal as written, for two independent reasons.

First, ClaimResolver.collect groups by exact Scala value equality at resolve.scala:333-345 and counts agreeing providers on that exact value. Boundary proposals at adjacent token gaps become two disagreements, even if the boundary model says they are one tolerance neighborhood.

Second, resolving individual boundaries independently cannot prove a globally lawful plan. Several accepted boundary values can jointly violate minimum-cell, ordering, eligibility, gap, or compatibility laws.

Reuse AgentProposal, evidence, receipts, raw-score discipline, and ResolutionState where they fit. Do not claim wholesale reuse of the resolver. Boundary construction needs:
1. a declared coordinate/dialect;
2. evidence-backed proposal clustering or explicit near-boundary equivalence;
3. a global plan resolver that selects or retains lawful sets;
4. a receipt for the equivalence and plan policy.

That clustering cannot be a caller-asserted cluster id. It must be derived, and exact provider agreement versus near agreement must remain distinguishable.

BLOCK 4 — S6 calls an uncalibrated family a marginal

Top-K Alternatives carry RawScore at most; acquire correctly refuses to turn those scores into probabilities. Without a calibrated distribution over JOINT boundary-plus-interpretation constructions, there is no expectation and no marginalization.

The first S6 output is therefore a labeled sensitivity family or envelope of complete HsmmResult/RecallSignature artifacts. Only a named calibration over the joint construction space licenses weighted expectations. Top-K selection itself must be receipted because omitted tail mass is unknown.

Also specify integration order. Visitation is nonlinear: 1 - exp(-columnMass). E_g[visitation_g] is not visitation(E_g[columnMass]). The plan must name which estimand it means. Transition flow can be averaged in shared source-edge coordinates. Transcript-span external mass needs an explicit base measure before it is commensurate.

A PATH THROUGH Q3

Compression and chronology do not require row-wise crosswalks if they are truly the same scalar estimand under each construction. Before calibration, publish the complete per-construction values and ranges with their supports. After joint calibration, publish E_g[T_g] plus within-construction and between-construction uncertainty, always averaging each COMPLETE per-construction estimand rather than P/F rows.

This does not automatically make the current definitions lawful. Chronology changes its n-1 step support under a split, and compression is row-mass based. The court must first establish that each scalar has a shared scientific meaning across admitted constructions. Q3 is an estimand-definition problem, not proof that no cross-cut answer can exist.

BLOCK 5 — S7 H2 points the wrong perturbations at the wrong quantities

A role reversal or polarity change should not necessarily move coverage, source visitation, or external mass. It should move the corresponding fidelity facet. Requiring every content mutation to move the same quantities would conflate truth/fidelity with salience/coverage, violating design rule 7.

Use matched, estimand-specific arms:
- omission changes coverage;
- source/external destination changes visitation or external mass;
- role, polarity, modality, and context mutations change their fidelity facets;
- order changes transition/chronology;
- granularity changes compression without awarding leaf detail.

For each arm preregister direction and delta. A constant fails sensitivity, but a metric should also fail if it moves for the wrong semantic coordinate.

H3 must split unweighted sensitivity value from calibrated marginal value. Retained uncalibrated alternatives can improve conclusion-change detection; they cannot win a calibration claim until calibration exists.

BLOCK 6 — reject I3 as stated

Hashing RecallUnitId from transcript identity plus span conflates an observation address with a hypothesis identity.

Two different claims may occupy the same words. One span may support competing interpretations. Overlapping claims make this ordinary, not exotic. Those objects would collide under I3. Conversely, cross-segmentation correspondence is a derived claim and must not become true merely because two ids are equal.

Keep graph-local object ids opaque. Introduce a separate stable transcript-span address for observations and a resolver-derived crosswalk for correspondence. A claim/hypothesis identity must include what distinguishes the hypothesis, not only where its evidence lies.

InterviewSegmenter's u7/ordinal-3 state proves ordinal-derived naming is misleading and perhaps a local contract defect. It does not prove span-derived object identity is the remedy. Fix the id contract only after deciding whether RecallUnitId means graph-local cell, persistent observation, or semantic claim.

SEQUENCING CHANGE

S1 may land independently as correctness. Before S2-S4, freeze the four-coordinate separation:
1. eligible transcript geometry;
2. boundary plan;
3. overlapping claims/interpretations;
4. construction authority and calibration.

Then build the 2x2 joint court and an unweighted sensitivity family. Calibrated marginalization and the lattice remain earned later.

This keeps the straw man's strongest sentence: recall construction is a resolver output, not a function return. It removes the places where the proposed remedy would create caller-selected classes, exact-equality boundary science, fake probabilities, and identity-by-location.

No vocabulary, ADR, bead, implementation, path, or reservation is claimed.
